refuted_block_candidates.candidate: CR/LF response splitting and ANSI/control-character injection via the caller-supplied X-Request-ID header
refuted_block_candidates.refutation: Live raw-socket probes: values containing CRLF, bare LF, an obs-fold continuation, ESC, NUL, BEL or VT are rejected by the HTTP parser with 400 before reaching the app (httptools 0.8.0; the h11 0.16 fallback validates field values equally strictly). Only tab and latin-1 high bytes pass, and both are legal header octets.

refuted_block_candidates.candidate: Log/JSON injection into the structured log stream via X-Request-ID
refuted_block_candidates.refutation: JSONLogFormatter renders through json.dumps with default ensure_ascii, so control and non-ASCII characters are escaped. Verified in the live log stream: tab and high bytes appear as escaped scalars inside a well-formed JSON line. No second record can be forged.

refuted_block_candidates.candidate: Stack trace or internal detail leaking on the 500 path after the move to pure-ASGI middleware
refuted_block_candidates.refutation: Driven live and in-process: the 500 body is plain-text 'Internal Server Error' (21 bytes). A seeded fake credential and absolute path in the exception message reached neither body nor headers, while X-Request-ID was still echoed (CR-003 fix verified).

refuted_block_candidates.candidate: Cross-request correlation-id bleed or collision with another request's id
refuted_block_candidates.refutation: 60 concurrent requests with distinct ids: every response echoed its own id and every id appears exactly once in the access log. The contextvar is per-task and reset in a finally. Residual risk is deliberate reuse by the caller, recorded as I3-VULN-002 (medium).

refuted_block_candidates.candidate: Unredacted PII in an access log line carrying a query string
refuted_block_candidates.refutation: uvicorn.access is disabled (not reformatted) and the middleware logs scope['path'] only. A request with a synthetic PAN and Aadhaar in the query string produced zero occurrences of either value in the log stream.

refuted_block_candidates.candidate: Redaction bypass via nested structures beyond a walk depth, or via extra= fields
refuted_block_candidates.refutation: The scrub runs on the rendered message, so arbitrarily nested dicts, lists, tuples and sets are covered - there is no walk depth. extra= fields are never emitted by the formatter at all, so they cannot leak.

refuted_block_candidates.candidate: Hostile input producing a wrong monetary value, precision loss, overflow or a pathological-Decimal DoS
refuted_block_candidates.refutation: Non-finite input rejected (CR-001 verified); unquantizable magnitudes fail closed with a typed error rather than truncating; a 1,000,000-digit input is rejected in 8 ms (linear); ROUND_HALF_UP is consistent and matches the frontend on negative ties; the wire form is always plain 2dp, never E-notation. Residual issues are validation laxity (I3-VULN-008) and a frontend formatting DoS (I3-VULN-009), both medium.

refuted_block_candidates.candidate: Critical/high npm advisories on vitest and vite in the changed manifest
refuted_block_candidates.refutation: All five advisories are devDependencies. No frontend build is deployed in this group; 'vitest run' never starts the UI/API server the critical advisory requires; vite.config.ts sets no server.host so the dev server binds localhost. Not reachable from the running application, so recorded as medium (I3-VULN-010) with the residual developer-workstation risk stated.

findings.title: Correlation id accepted unbounded and echoed into every log line
findings.detail: The inbound X-Request-ID is taken verbatim with no length cap or charset check, then echoed in the response header and in the request_id field of every log line. Verified live: a ~1 MB header produced a single 1,048,722-byte JSON log line and a 1 MB response header echo from one request. Amplification grows with the number of log lines per request, and no rate limiting exists.
findings.fix: Cap the accepted value at 64-128 characters, restrict it to [A-Za-z0-9._:-], and fall back to the generated uuid4().hex otherwise. Test that a 1 MB header yields a generated id and a bounded log line.

findings.title: Caller-supplied correlation id is trusted and indistinguishable from a generated one
findings.detail: A client-supplied 32-hex-character value is echoed and logged exactly as a server-generated uuid4().hex would be, with nothing marking it as caller-supplied. An attacker can reuse a known id so an investigation cannot separate two actors, or flood the logs with legitimate-looking ids. No cross-request contamination (tested), so impact is confined to log attribution - but the log stream is this platform's audit substrate.
findings.fix: Always generate the server-side id and keep the inbound value in a separate client_request_id field (preserving the E15-S1-AC3 echo), or validate its shape and flag caller-supplied ids in the log payload.

findings.title: PII redaction is scope-bound and bypassed by the exception path
findings.detail: RedactionFilter scrubs only values registered via redact_values(...) and only while that scope is on the stack. The scope unwinds during exception propagation, so an outer layer logging afterwards sees an empty sensitive-value set. Reproduced in-process exactly as uvicorn logs an unhandled exception: an exception message carrying a synthetic PAN, raised inside a redact_values scope, was emitted at ERROR with the PAN intact (and request_id empty). Compounding this, no production call site for redact_values exists, so E15-S1-AC1 passes only because its own test registers the values it asserts absent. Not a BLOCK at HEAD because group A exposes only GET /health and no code path carries applicant data; becomes a data-exposure BLOCK when the first PII-accepting endpoint lands.
findings.fix: Add format-based redaction (PAN/Aadhaar/account-number patterns) in RedactionFilter as scope-independent defense in depth, and/or register the request's sensitive values in CorrelationIdMiddleware so the scope spans the unwind. Test that a PII-bearing exception escaping a handler reaches the sink redacted.

findings.title: Redaction misses transformed representations of a registered value
findings.detail: Only whitespace and hyphens are tolerated between characters. Verified by probe: the same registered value written with dots, underscores or slashes, URL-encoded, or base64-encoded passes through unredacted. Base64 is the concrete risk for the 'salary-document content' this story names. Separately, any registered value shorter than 6 characters is silently never redacted.
findings.fix: Normalize the haystack (strip non-alphanumerics, casefold) and match the normalized needle, mapping matches back to the original span; at minimum widen the separator class. Warn or raise when a registered value is too short to be redactable.

findings.title: Error context mapping is an unfiltered outbound channel
findings.detail: AppError.context is typed Mapping[str, object] and copied verbatim into the response body with no allowlist, key or type restriction, and no redaction (RedactionFilter covers the log sink only, so a value scrubbed from logs still ships to the client). Verified: SQL text, an absolute source path and a nested config mapping all arrived intact in the JSON body. No production subclass populates context at HEAD, so nothing internal leaks today - but the frozen contract invites population (E4-S4-AC2 needs threshold_kind and configured_value there). The detail field carries the same exposure for free-form messages.
findings.fix: Give each AppError subclass a declared typed context (TypedDict or model) restricted to primitive values and build the response from that declaration. Test that the envelope cannot carry filesystem paths, SQL fragments or unexpected keys.

findings.title: Non-JSON-serializable context turns the intended error into a 500
findings.detail: JSONResponse serializes context with no coercion. Verified: an AppError raised with status_code=422 and a Decimal in context produced a plain-text 500 instead - the TypeError escapes the handler into ServerErrorMiddleware, losing the status code, error name, detail and the frozen envelope. Likely first-contact failure, since configured_value in the contract is a money threshold and money is Decimal here; the existing test passes only because it uses the string '25000.00'.
findings.fix: Coerce or validate context values to JSON primitives in AppError.__init__ or in the handler, and test the handler with a Decimal and a Money in context.

findings.title: Interactive docs and OpenAPI schema enabled unconditionally and unauthenticated
findings.detail: Verified live: /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json all return 200 with no authentication. Today the schema discloses only /health and the service name, but the factory has no environment switch, so the full API surface becomes public the moment group B adds routes. /docs is also HTML that loads scripts and CSS from cdn.jsdelivr.net, adding a third-party script dependency to a pure JSON service.
findings.fix: Pass docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None unless an explicit setting (e.g. TRUELEND_ENABLE_DOCS, default off) enables them, and test that the three paths 404 under default settings.

findings.title: Money wire parser accepts far more than the frozen format, with no magnitude bound
findings.detail: Decision D-G fixes the wire form as a quoted 2dp string, but both sides hand the string straight to a decimal constructor. Verified: the backend field accepts leading/trailing whitespace, underscore digit separators, scientific notation and a leading '+', and accepts 26 integer digits - which the NUMERIC(14,2) column D-G specifies cannot store, so the value validates at the API boundary and fails later at the database. The two sides also disagree on validity: whitespace-padded input is backend-accepted and frontend-rejected, while a 101-digit magnitude is frontend-accepted and backend-rejected. Related files: backend/src/types/money.py:59, frontend/src/types/money.ts:24.
findings.fix: Enforce ^-?\d{1,12}(\.\d{1,2})?$ in _validate_money and in toQuantizedDecimal before constructing the decimal, with matching negative tests on both sides.

findings.title: Quadratic grouping regex in Money.format() is a main-thread DoS
findings.detail: The thousands-separator regex uses a repeated group inside a lookahead evaluated at every position, quadratic in digit count. Measured in node: 10k digits 37 ms, 50k digits 1.01 s, 200k digits 18.7 s of synchronous main-thread work. Money.fromWire accepts a 100k-digit string in 3.4 ms, and MoneyTextProps.money is declared Money | string, so the component will parse and format an unvalidated string. Only the backend produces money strings today (capped at 28 digits) and MoneyText is not yet rendered by any page, hence WARN; reachable as soon as a money string originates from or is echoed back from user input. Related: frontend/src/ui/components/MoneyText.tsx:13.
findings.fix: Bound the integer-digit count at parse time (see I3-VULN-008) and replace the grouping regex with a linear loop or Intl.NumberFormat.

findings.title: Vulnerable dev dependencies: vitest (critical advisory) and vite (high advisory)
findings.detail: npm audit on the changed manifest reports 5 advisories (1 critical, 1 high, 3 moderate): vitest ^2.0.5 (vulnerable <=4.1.10) GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp arbitrary file read/exec while the Vitest UI server listens, plus GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9; vite ^5.4.3 (vulnerable <=6.4.2) GHSA-4w7w-66w2-5vf9 path traversal in optimized-deps .map handling, GHSA-v6wh-96g9-6wx3 launch-editor NTLMv2 hash disclosure via UNC paths on Windows, GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff server.fs.deny bypass; moderate esbuild, @vitest/mocker, vite-node. Refuted to medium: devDependencies only, no deployed frontend build in this group, 'vitest run' never starts the UI/API server, dev server binds localhost. Residual risk is to a developer workstation running npm run dev on Windows. Backend dependencies are clean at the installed versions (fastapi 0.141.1, starlette 1.6.0, uvicorn 0.52.4, pydantic 2.13.5, h11 0.16.0).
findings.fix: Bump vite and vitest out of the vulnerable ranges (npm reports vite@8.3.0 and vitest@5.0.0 as the available fixes, both semver-major) or pin patched versions, then re-audit.

findings.title: No hardening response headers; server product disclosed
findings.detail: No X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/CSP frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy or HSTS on any response, and 'server: uvicorn' is advertised. Mostly moot for a JSON API with no cookies or browser auth yet, but /docs returns HTML with no CSP while loading third-party scripts.
findings.fix: Add a small response-header middleware (and suppress the server header) when the UI surface lands.

findings.title: Registered PII values persist in a process-global cache
findings.detail: _redaction_pattern is an lru_cache(maxsize=256) keyed on the sensitive value, so up to 256 PAN/Aadhaar/document values stay resident as cache keys and inside compiled patterns long after their redaction scope ends, and would appear in a heap dump or core file.
findings.fix: Key the cache on a hash, drop the cache and accept the compile cost, or clear it when the scope exits.

findings.title: extra= fields are silently discarded by the formatter
findings.detail: The JSON payload is a fixed five-key shape, so logger.info(..., extra={...}) is dropped. Leak-safe today, but a developer who believes extra is recorded may place PII there and reason about it incorrectly, and structured context cannot be logged at all.
findings.fix: Merge an allowlisted set of extras through the same scrub, or document the omission.

findings.title: The stack-trace line for a 500 carries an empty request_id
findings.detail: The contextvar is reset before uvicorn logs the unhandled exception, so the one line containing the traceback is uncorrelated (request_id: ''), as observed in the live log. The middleware's own access line does carry the id and the real status, so E15-S1-AC4 holds.
findings.fix: Log the exception inside the middleware scope, or have the handler read the id from the ASGI scope.

findings.title: The public error code is a Python class name
findings.detail: error is type(self).__name__, so an internal class rename silently changes the wire contract and a class named after an internal component publishes that name. The frozen contract does require an error name, so this is not a leak in itself.
findings.fix: Declare an explicit error_code class attribute per subclass and assert the set of codes in a test.

findings.title: No secret-handling convention in Settings
findings.detail: Nothing is hardcoded and no dotenv is read (env_file is not configured, contrary to the docstring hint), but the docstring says DB URL and JWT settings land in this same class later, and nothing would stop a future logger.info('%s', settings) from dumping them since the model repr prints all fields.
findings.fix: Adopt pydantic.SecretStr for every credential field and add a test asserting repr(Settings()) contains no secret value.

findings.title: TRUELEND_LOG_LEVEL is unvalidated
findings.detail: An invalid value fails startup (acceptable fail-fast); DEBUG in production widens log content while redaction is still opt-in.
findings.fix: Constrain the field to the standard level names with a Literal.

findings.title: Sub-cent amounts are silently accepted as zero
findings.detail: 1e-400 and 0.004 are accepted and quantize to 0.00. Correct 2dp rounding, but a future minimum-amount or non-zero check must run after quantization or it will pass a value later stored as zero.
findings.fix: Reject inputs with non-zero digits below the second decimal place, or document the rounding contract at the API boundary.

findings.title: Frontend decimal context relies on a mutable library default
findings.detail: Rounding is passed explicitly at every call site, but Decimal.precision is never set, so the module inherits decimal.js's default 20 significant digits - and Decimal.set() is process-global, so any other module sharing the instance can change money arithmetic app-wide. Results at 2dp are unaffected for NUMERIC(14,2) magnitudes, so this is hardening only.
findings.fix: Create a configured Decimal clone for this module.
